lockFileMaintenance.description: Refresh the committed lockfiles on a schedule so transitive advisories get fixed. Renovate only proposes updates for the direct declarations it manages, so a vulnerable package that no manifest names is never reached by an ordinary update or by a vulnerability alert, and its advisory stays open until the lockfile is regenerated. The Friday early-morning window matches the maintainer's preference for scheduled dependency work, and automerge matches the non-major automerge policy: required status checks still gate the merge, so a refresh that breaks a check stays open for review.

customManagers.description: Keep the pinned Renovate config validator and its regression expectation in lockstep so CI never resolves a moving toolchain.

The commitlint versions pinned inline in the commitlint workflow and in scripts/commitlint-local. No built-in manager reads a version out of a shell script or a workflow run step, and the two must move together or a local check disagrees with CI.

Renovate's docker datasource reads release timestamps only from Docker Hub, so under timestamp-required every .NET SDK digest update would stay pending forever. The mcr-dotnet-sdk feed supplies the time MCR last pushed each tag and the tag's current digest; see ADR 0125.

BetterLeaks publishes its image only on GHCR, where Renovate's docker datasource reads no release timestamps, so timestamp-required would hold every update forever. The betterleaks-ghcr feed supplies the timestamp and the manifest digest for each version; see ADR 0124.

The FROM line pins a digest without a tag; the digest is a build OSS-Fuzz tagged v1. The oss-fuzz-base-builder-jvm feed offers the newest v1 build pushed at least seven days ago as release v1, so Renovate replaces only the digest. See ADR 0126.
The oss-fuzz-clusterfuzzlite-run-fuzzers feed offers the newest v1 build pushed at least seven days ago as release v1, so Renovate replaces only the digest and keeps the v1 tag. See ADR 0126.

betterleaks-ghcr.description: GitHub's newest 100 package-version records for ghcr.io/betterleaks/betterleaks. Every exact vX.Y.Z tag becomes release X.Y.Z with the record's created_at as its release timestamp and the record's manifest digest. Release candidates, the v1 alias, latest and sha256-* signature tags are left out.

mcr-dotnet-sdk.description: Microsoft Artifact Registry's tag catalog for mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk. Every major.minor tag, such as 8.0, becomes a release with the catalog's lastModifiedDate, the time MCR last pushed that tag, as its release timestamp and the tag's current manifest-list digest. Patch, distribution and architecture tags are left out because the pin follows a major.minor tag.

oss-fuzz-base-builder-jvm.description: Artifact Registry's newest 1,000 versions of gcr.io/oss-fuzz-base/base-builder-jvm. OSS-Fuzz pushes three builds a day: the v1 build, tagged v1 and latest, and the ubuntu-20-04 and ubuntu-24-04 builds with one tag each. Pushing a one-tag build moves the tag off the previous build in the same write, so the previous build's updateTime equals the new build's createTime. A v1 build moves its second tag minutes after the push, so the v1 builds are the image manifests whose createTime is no other version's updateTime. The newest v1 build pushed at least seven days ago becomes release v1 with its createTime and digest. The lookup fails if the newest build the rule selects is not the one tagged v1.

($release := $newest($lineage[$toMillis(createTime) <= $millis() - $minimumAgeMs]); {"releases": $exists($release) ? [{"version": "v1", "releaseTimestamp": $release.createTime, "digest": $substringAfter($release.name, "/versions/")}] : [], "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz"}) : $error("The newest base-builder-jvm image the v1-build rule selects does not carry the v1 tag; see ADR 0126."))

oss-fuzz-clusterfuzzlite-run-fuzzers.description: Artifact Registry's newest 1,000 versions of gcr.io/oss-fuzz-base/clusterfuzzlite-run-fuzzers. Each OSS-Fuzz build pushes the v1 image and then the ubuntu-24-04 image, 0.5 to 2 seconds apart, and separate builds are more than 8 seconds apart. Both images carry two tags, so the update times do not tell them apart. The v1 builds are the image manifests that start such a pair: the previous image manifest is more than 5 seconds older and the next one at most 5 seconds newer. The newest v1 build pushed at least seven days ago becomes release v1 with its createTime and digest. The lookup fails if the newest build the rule selects is not the one tagged v1.

($release := $newest($lineage[$toMillis(createTime) <= $millis() - $minimumAgeMs]); {"releases": $exists($release) ? [{"version": "v1", "releaseTimestamp": $release.createTime, "digest": $substringAfter($release.name, "/versions/")}] : [], "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz"}) : $error("The newest clusterfuzzlite-run-fuzzers image the v1-build rule selects does not carry the v1 tag; see ADR 0126."))

packageRules.description: Public repository: merge eligible non-major updates after checks pass. Group only dependencies that need coordinated updates; keep unrelated updates separate.

prBodyNotes: Automation validates this dependency-only update and runs the ordered OpenRewrite and Spotless pipeline.
When an eligible non-major update produces no repository change, required CI passes and Renovate automerges this pull request.
When the toolchain changes source or POM output, this pull request remains blocked and automation opens or refreshes a separate generated pull request for maintainer review.
Major updates are created automatically and require manual merge through the repository-wide major-update guard.
Quarkus updater recipe changes MUST NOT be validated as general OpenRewrite maintenance updates.
Before merge, a maintainer MUST review the target Quarkus migration guide, run `quarkus:update` in the dependency-update branch, review the complete diff, and pass the full Maven gate.
After Renovate updates `tessl.json`, run `tessl install`, review the refreshed `.tessl/tiles` diff, and commit those vendored tile changes before merging.

packageRules.description: Major updates require human review of migration notes. Preserve compatibility groups whose members must move together across a major boundary.

The OSS-Fuzz custom managers own these FROM lines. The dockerfile manager would look the images up through the docker datasource, which has no release timestamps for gcr.io, and add a second digest update that stays pending forever. See ADR 0126.

A new OSS-Fuzz v1 build turns seven days old every day, so without a window each of these two images would get an automerged digest pull request every day. They use the Friday early-morning window of lockFileMaintenance instead, one pull request per image per week. The seven-day wait and automerge apply as to every digest update. See ADR 0126.
